title: One-Pot French Onion Pasta
subtitle: One pot · torched cheese top
description: Orecchiette cooked straight in beef broth with jammy caramelized onions and crispy pancetta, finished with cream, parmesan and a blistered cheese top.

steps.text: Heat the {{oil}} in a large, deep pan over medium heat. Add the {{onions}} with a pinch of {{salt}} and cook, stirring now and then, until deeply golden and jammy. Whenever a brown crust builds on the pan, add a splash of water and scrape it back in.
Push the onions to one side, add the {{pancetta}} to the empty side and fry until crisp, then stir everything together. Add the {{garlic}} and cook for a minute until fragrant.
Pour in the {{wine}}, scraping up any browned bits, and simmer until mostly evaporated.

Add the {{pasta}}, {{broth}}, {{thyme}} and plenty of {{pepper}}. Simmer, stirring often so nothing sticks, until the pasta is al dente and the liquid is a glossy sauce. Top up with a little water if it dries out first.
Turn the heat to low and stir in the {{cream}}, then the {{parmesan}} a handful at a time until melted and the sauce coats the pasta.

Scatter the {{gruyere}} over the top and cover briefly to melt, then blister it with a kitchen torch (or 2–3 minutes under a hot grill if the pan is oven-safe). Garnish with thyme and serve from the pan.

notes: Quantities follow standard French onion pasta ratios — the source video doesn't show measurements, so adjust to taste.
Don't rush the onions; the deep caramelization is the whole flavor base.
Gruyère is the classic French onion choice, but low-moisture mozzarella melts and torches beautifully too.
